title: Scripture: one God adored and served; the Roman reply of latria and dulia
source_text: LXXI. Sed ut ad Sacram Scripturam redeamus, non solum in ea nullum praeceptum aut exemplum de Angelorum, sive de Sanctorum mortuorum cultu reperitur, sed saepius ipsa docet unum Deum adorandum, & illi soli serviendum esse: adeoque nec Angelis, nec Sanctis in Christo defunctis religiosum ullum cultum esse deferendum. Respondent Scholae Romanae Doctores scripturam solum prohibere ne creaturis deferamus cultum illum summum atque absolutum, quo aliquis colitur, tanquam primum principium, atque ultimus finis, cui cultui Latriae nomen appropriaverunt, non vero prohibitum esse Dei Ministris & amicis, quales sunt Angeli, & justorum Spiritus in gloriam caelestem recepti, inferiorem illum religionis cultum quem ipsi Duliam appellant, exhibere.
pass_a_gloss: But to return to Sacred Scripture, not only is no precept or example found in it concerning the worship of Angels or of dead Saints, but more often it itself teaches that one God is to be adored and that he alone is to be served: and so that no religious worship is to be offered either to Angels or to Saints who have died in Christ. The Doctors of the Roman School respond that scripture only forbids that we offer to creatures that highest and absolute worship by which someone is worshipped as first principle and last end, to which worship they have appropriated the name of Latria; but that it is not forbidden to show to God's Ministers and friends, such as are the Angels and the Spirits of the just received into heavenly glory, that lower worship of religion which they themselves call Dulia.
pass_b_english: But to return to Holy Scripture: not only does it contain no command or example concerning the worship of angels or of the dead saints, but it often teaches that one God is to be adored and that he alone is to be served. So no religious worship at all is to be given either to angels or to the saints who have died in Christ.

The teachers of the Roman school reply that Scripture forbids us only to give creatures that supreme and absolute worship by which someone is worshiped as first principle and last end, the worship for which they have reserved the name latria. It does not, they say, forbid us to show God's servants and friends, such as the angels and the spirits of the just received into heavenly glory, that lower religious worship which they call dulia.

lemmas.gloss: to which worship they have appropriated the name Latria

choices.why: The Roman doctors restrict the word latria to supreme worship; 'reserved' gives the sense of claiming the term for one use only.
